## What the warning means

This `FutureWarning` was introduced in SciPy 1.14.0. bootstrap will now emit a FutureWarning if the shapes of the elements of data are not the same (with the exception of the dimension specified by axis).

More specifically, per the 1.15.0 release notes: scipy.stats.bootstrap now emits a FutureWarning if the shapes of the input arrays do not agree. Broadcast the arrays to the same batch shape (i.e. for all dimensions except those specified by the axis argument) to avoid the warning.

## Why it happens

When you pass multiple samples in `data` to `bootstrap`, SciPy requires that Elements of data must be broadcastable to the same shape (with the possible exception of the dimension specified by axis).

The message "Ignoring the dimension specified by `axis`" refers to the fact that all dimensions *except* the `axis` dimension must match/broadcast. The `axis` dimension is the one along which the statistic is computed and is allowed to differ between samples. If your input arrays have mismatched shapes in the *non-axis* dimensions, the warning fires.

## How to fix it

Broadcast the arrays to the same batch shape (i.e. for all dimensions except those specified by the axis argument) to avoid the warning. Broadcasting will be performed automatically in the future.

In practice, you should manually broadcast (e.g., with `np.broadcast_arrays` or `np.broadcast_to`) your input samples so they share the same shape in every dimension except `axis` before passing them to `bootstrap`.

## Future behavior

Beginning in SciPy 1.16.0, bootstrap will explicitly broadcast the elements to the same shape (except along axis). So in newer versions the broadcasting is handled automatically, and the warning goes away.

**Note on the underlying cause:** This warning was added to address silent bugs. As described in the related SciPy issue, when a statistic depends on multiple mismatched-shape samples, Calculating `statistic(*resampled_data, axis=-1)` will fail, due to a dimension mismatch. In some other examples, it will fail silently, which can be worse, causing errors that propagate into downstream statistical analyses.

If you're seeing this warning, the safest fix is to ensure all your `data` arrays have matching shapes (except along `axis`), or simply upgrade to SciPy 1.16.0+ where the broadcasting is done for you.
